description: Detects infrastructure, tooling, or architectural complexity added before the bottleneck is proven or the core loop is validated
warning_signs: Adding a message queue (Kafka, RabbitMQ, Celery, BullMQ) before proving async load is a real bottleneck
Adding a caching layer (Redis, Memcached, CDN cache) before measuring what is slow
Adding microservices or service splits before single-node pain exists
Adding orchestration (Kubernetes, Docker Compose multi-service) before stable core logic
Adding a vector DB or embedding pipeline before validating retrieval quality
Adding auth/user systems before proving the core loop works end-to-end
Adding background workers before synchronous path is validated
Adding rate limiting / API gateway before load is measured
Adding observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, datadog) before core loop is stable
Adding multi-region or HA infrastructure before users are acquired
rubric: Is there explicit evidence in project memory (goal, milestone, constraint, or decision) of a bottleneck that requires this component?
Is the current milestone blocked without this component? Would the milestone fail its success metric without it?
Does this component increase the operational or debugging surface significantly (adds ~2+ new moving parts)?
Is a simpler, local-first alternative available that could validate the same thing at this stage?
Does this change contradict a prior decision record or an explicit constraint in memory?
good_warning_examples: You added Redis caching, but your milestone is proving retrieval quality and no eval baseline exists yet. This adds infra before evidence. What bottleneck does this solve right now?
This introduces an async worker queue, but your goal states 'validate single-user flow first.' The synchronous path hasn't been proven yet — what failure mode does this prevent?
You added Kafka, but your constraint says 'no distributed systems before single-node pain.' What measured load metric justified introducing a message broker at this stage?
A vector DB was added before your RAG retrieval quality has been evaluated. Your current milestone is retrieval validation — adding Pinecone now makes evaluation harder, not easier.
bad_warning_examples: Consider whether this is the best approach.
You might want to think about scalability.
This could be improved with better architecture.
Have you considered using a different pattern?
Redis is often overkill for small projects.
Make sure you need this before adding it.
